newsitem.title: USA: Washington mayor says he is forced to make cuts.
newsitem.headline: Washington mayor says he is forced to make cuts.

text.p: Mayor Marion Barry said Sunday the Federal Control Board was forcing him to cut $50 million from his spending plans to help balance the capital's budget.
Barry has resisted spending cuts, arguing that further cutbacks would hurt city residents who already face a loss of services from earlier reductions in spending.

Asked on NBC Television's "Meet the Press" if he would go along with the control board's demands, Barry said: "Well, I'm being forced to because the board won't let us restructure, and we're going to have to cut out these valuable and good services.

"I don't want to do that," he said. "We ought to do what New York did. They refinanced that debt the first year. Philadelphia did the same thing. Cleveland did the same thing. What's wrong with Washington?"
Barry complained that Congress had prevented him from taxing commuters from Maryland and Virginia suburbs in the same way that other cities tax commuters.
